# Fake replacement map

<!-- generated by `cargo xtask replacement-map` from conformance/replacement-map.json; do not edit -->

This file maps every conformance id, every R-1.4 fault and every Core error code to the proof that replaces its frozen fake. BUILD.md "Testing architecture" says that nothing fake is deleted before this map is reviewed and the replacement is green.

Prior art: the steward's assessment (`~/botster-sessions/shared/fake-mode-steward-assessment.md`), BUILD.md "Testing architecture", and Core Amendment 5 candidate 4 (A5-1 to A5-4) and Hub→client Amendment 5 candidate 2. Both amendments are accepted (manifest final12). This map follows them. The service-lane edge, the retained `Cancelled` code and the `Internal` proof are open steward items.

Each id was classified by reading its clause. The `edge` and the `note` of each entry are in `conformance/replacement-map.json`. `cargo xtask replacement-map --check` runs in CI. It fails when an id, a fault or a Core error code is missing, when a proof is outside the closed set, or when this file is stale.

## Proof kinds (the closed set)

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `core-testkit` | real Core in-process (botster-core-testkit: in-process worker, scripted program backend, real libghostty) |
| `core-testkit+edge` | as above, with an edge fault: storage, program-backend, process (including the withheld control link, Core A6-1), service-lane (Core A6-1), route-transport, wake or clock |
| `core-testkit+perturb` | as above, under seeded variation produced at its source: the testkit scheduler and edges (Core A5-2: OR-1..OR-3, batching, coalescing, partial pumps) |
| `hub-inproc` | the real Hub in-process over the in-memory transport, with the testkit under it |
| `hub-inproc+edge` | as above, with an edge fault: transport, storage, plugin-loader, clock, network, process or filesystem |
| `hub-inproc+perturb` | as above, under seeded variation: the Hub scheduler for producer variations and the permute-only transport decorator for delivery variations (HC A5-4: EN-3, WT-7, TS-3, TR-3, resync placement) |
| `player:client` | the client-subject runner plays the Hub from the transcript (client boundary checks; Web through the TS player) |
| `player:hp-frame` | FakePlugin or the plugin-side FakeHub as a frame-script player (HP section 19) |
| `real:lua-host` | the real Lua host as the subject, with the HP FakeHub frame-script player as its peer |
| `real:cli` | the real CLI as the subject, with the transcript player as the Hub |
| `realize` | the reference realize (already real code) |
| `static` | a check in the contract crates or xtask with no Core, Hub, player or fake: generated-artifact drift, a compile test, or a crate-layout or path check |
| `slow:<reason>` | a named real-process test in the slow tier |
| `deferred:<reason>` | a proof the contract defers until a named release condition (Core A6-2); the note gives the end condition |
| `withdrawn` | an id that a ruling withdrew and replaced (Core A9-2): it has no proof, and its note names the authority and the replacement (conformance/withdrawn.txt) |

Edges: Core edges are `storage`, `program-backend` (the scripted program), `process` (spawning or ending a worker, guardian or service, A5-1; and, from Core A6-1, keeping a worker alive while it withholds its control link until after the deadline, which gives `WorkerUnreachable`), `service-lane` (Core A6-1: a scripted service over in-memory lanes, with the real preamble and epoch checks), `route-transport`, `wake` (a spurious wake, A5-1) and `clock` (the host passes `now`, TM-1; the testkit adds no clock). Hub edges are `transport`, `storage`, `plugin-loader`, `clock`, `network` (the scripted I/O service, MCP server, DNS and git source), `process` and `filesystem`.

## R-1.4 faults

Each fault is injected through an edge, the perturbation layer or the player. The Hub side and the client side are separate proofs.

| Fault | Clauses | Side | Proof | How |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| drop the transport mid-route | HC TS-9, HC TS-11 | hub | `hub-inproc+edge:transport` | The transport edge cuts the connection while a route is attached; the player scripts the same cut for a client. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| plugin reload between describe and dispatch | HC DS-6 | hub | `hub-inproc+edge:plugin-loader` | The plugin-loader edge reloads the plugin after a describe answer and before the dispatch. |
| drop a committed response | HC EN-7, HC EN-8 | hub | `hub-inproc+edge:transport` | The transport edge drops the response frame after the Hub committed the effect. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| concurrent duplicate idempotency keys | HC EN-8 | hub | `hub-inproc+perturb` | The Hub scheduler orders two concurrent requests with one key (a producer variation, HC A5-4); the clause does not fix the order. |
| resync while a frame is partly written, and a started frame that cannot finish | codec TS-4c, codec TS-9 | worker | `core-testkit+edge:route-transport` | The route-transport edge stalls or cuts a write inside a frame. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| unknown verb or component | HC EN-6 | hub | `hub-inproc` | A raw frame with an unknown verb is a plain stimulus; the player sends an unknown component to a client. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| internal queue loss on a watch | HC WT-4 | hub | `hub-inproc+edge:transport` | A stalled transport edge fills the per-watch queue; the player scripts the resulting resync for a client. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| a resync that discards notifications so that output_dropped occurs | codec TS-4c, HC SF-5f | worker | `core-testkit+edge:route-transport` | The route-transport edge stalls a reader until the worker resyncs; real libghostty finds the notifications. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |
| every seeded interleaving point of HC section 12 | HC EN-3, HC WT-3, HC WT-7, HC WT-8, HC TS-3, HC TS-9, HC TR-3 | hub | `hub-inproc+perturb` | HC A5-4: producer variations come from the Hub scheduler (real Hub) or scripted alternatives (player); delivery variations from the permute-only transport decorator. |
| | | client | `player:client` | |

## Core error codes

Core Amendment 5 candidate 4 (A5-3) says every code is reached at its own timing: a scripted synchronous refusal before admission, an edge for an asynchronous failure, or a `CoreLimits` value; a code that only the OS produces is a named real-process test. `call` is an ordinary call with a bad argument or state: it needs no injection. `unit` is a static check with a reason.

| Code | How | Edge or limit | Proof | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UnknownSession` | call |  | `core-testkit` | A call names an id that no session has (conf::er_unknown_session). |
| `UnknownRoute` | call |  | `core-testkit` | A call names a route id that no route has. |
| `IdTooLong` | limit | max_session_id_bytes | `core-testkit` | Create with an id over the limit (ID-1). |
| `IdInUse` | call |  | `core-testkit` | Create with an existing id (LC-3). |
| `WrongState` | call |  | `core-testkit` | Sync form: a call in a state that forbids it. Async form: the perturbation orders a state change before the completion. |
| `SessionEnded` | edge | program-backend | `core-testkit+edge` | Async on Signal, SetSizePolicy and Resize (A2-1): the scripted program exits while the operation is deferred (A5-2), so the operation completes with this code. WriteInput never returns it (A2-2); the IN-7 write outcome is an InputResult and belongs to the IN-7 ids, not to this row. |
| `MissingWorkerPath` | call |  | `core-testkit` | open without a worker path (LC-1). |
| `DataDirInUse` | real-only |  | `slow:data-dir-lock` | The exclusive lock on the data directory is a real file lock (LC-2). |
| `StartFailed` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | See the start-failure reasons below. |
| `WorkerLinkFailed` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | Async on Signal, SetSizePolicy, SetColorProfile, SetOutputTap, the reads, CaptureSnapshot and Resize (A2-1): the process edge ends the worker at a script point while the operation is deferred (A5-2). WriteInput never returns it (A2-2). |
| `LaneFull` | limit | input_ops_per_session, input_retained_bytes | `core-testkit` | A small input bound (IN-5). |
| `InvalidInput` | call |  | `core-testkit` | A malformed semantic input (IN-9). |
| `PayloadTooLarge` | limit | max_paste_bytes | `core-testkit` | A payload over the paste bound (IN-5). |
| `PendingLimit` | limit | pending_ops | `core-testkit` | A small pending_ops, with no completion polled (EV-5a). |
| `SessionLimit` | limit | max_sessions | `core-testkit` |  |
| `RouteLimit` | limit | routes_per_session | `core-testkit` |  |
| `CaptureLimit` | limit | open_captures_per_client | `core-testkit` | CaptureSnapshot past the bound (ST-6). |
| `ServiceLimit` | limit | max_services | `core-testkit` |  |
| `Cancelled` | call |  | `core-testkit` | OPEN STEWARD ITEM: the A2-1 table lists no operation that returns Cancelled (cancel applies to WriteInput only, and A2-2 gives WriteInput an InputResult outcome). The proof is provisional until the steward rules whether Cancelled is retained and which operation returns it. |
| `CursorReadUnsupported` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | A2-1: it means no worker model for the session. The process edge reports a worker with no model at ReadScreen, ReadCursor, ReadModeFlags, CaptureSnapshot or ReadFacts (async). Reads of a Created or Lost session are sync WrongState, not this code. It is not an N-1 worker case (AD-4). |
| `UnknownCapture` | call |  | `core-testkit` |  |
| `PageOutOfRange` | call |  | `core-testkit` |  |
| `Unsupported` | call |  | `core-testkit` | A feature that features() does not list, or a worker that lacks it (AD-4). |
| `InvalidConfig` | limit | any CoreLimits value zero or out of range | `core-testkit` | open with a bad limit (9B). |
| `RegistryFailed` | edge | storage | `core-testkit+edge` | The storage edge fails a write, including the write-ahead row (AD-7); the uncertain form (RegistryFailed{uncertain: true}) is a separate script: the write has an unknown effect. |
| `SnapshotTooLarge` | limit | max_snapshot_bytes | `core-testkit` | A small max_snapshot_bytes, with route_queue_bytes at least that value (9B), and a screen model whose snapshot exceeds it. CaptureSnapshot completes with this code (A2-1, ST-6); an attach baseline closes the route typed (OU-9). |
| `BoundUnavailable` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | The process edge reports a required bound as not applicable (SV-4). |
| `Internal` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | OPEN STEWARD ITEM: A2-1 lists no sync Internal, and A2-2 gives WriteInput Internal as its only async error, but no clause names the edge that produces it (A5-3 item 2 allows an async code only through an edge). The proof is provisional until the steward names the edge or rules a unit proof. |
| `UnknownService` | call |  | `core-testkit` |  |
| `StartFailed:ExecFailed` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | The process edge refuses exec with an errno. |
| `StartFailed:CwdMissing` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | A missing working directory (A2-1). |
| `StartFailed:StartupTimeout` | edge | clock | `core-testkit+edge` | The scripted worker never answers; the host passes a later now (LC-4). |
| `StartFailed:WorkerFailed` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` |  |
| `StartFailed:GuardianFailed` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` |  |
| `StartFailed:Other` | unit |  | `static` | The non-exhaustive fallback value; a reader maps an unknown reason to Other (contract crate round trip). |

| `Lost:WorkerVersion` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | Core A6-2: the real worker announces a hello number outside the adoptable set; only the version check is under test. No old protocol is fabricated (AD-4). |
| `Lost:RegistryCorrupt` | edge | storage | `core-testkit+edge` |  |
| `Lost:StartInterrupted` | edge | storage | `core-testkit+edge` | A Starting row with no recorded identity (AD-1). |
| `Lost:GuardianLost` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | The process edge ends the guardian; where the OS kills the service with it, the real-only part is slow:pdeathsig (SV-8). |
| `Lost:EpochExhausted` | edge | process | `core-testkit+edge` | A scripted service sends the largest epoch (SV-6). |
| `Lost:Other` | unit |  | `static` | The non-exhaustive fallback value. |

## Deferred

2 ids have no subject yet (Core A6-2). Each note gives the end condition.

- `ad_4_missing_worker_capability_is_unsupported` (`deferred:worker-protocol-2`): Core A6-2: deferred until the first release whose protocol T adds a worker feature that the pinned T-1 worker lacks; its subject is that feature. A release that adds no worker feature does not end the deferral.
- `ad_4_previous_worker_version_adopts` (`deferred:worker-protocol-2`): Core A6-2: deferred until the first release whose protocol T is 2. It then runs a pinned protocol-1 worker binary under that Core (a slow run). No old protocol is fabricated.

## Ids whose current proof is a frozen fake

The frozen fakes are FakeCore and the fake route endpoint. There is no FakeHub: a `hub` transcript runs against the real Hub in Stage 2 (HC A5-1), and in Phase 0 it gets a structural check only. An id has a current fake proof when its transcript has the subject `core` or `worker` and is not marked `fake: structural`. A structural transcript (R-5, R-7) is checked only for its structure; it is not a fake behavior proof, so the table leaves it out and counts it below. An id with no transcript yet has no current proof. The fakes stay unchanged until the replacement is green.

## Open steward items

These 2 Core error codes have a provisional proof, because the steward has not ruled.

- `Cancelled` (`core-testkit`): OPEN STEWARD ITEM: the A2-1 table lists no operation that returns Cancelled (cancel applies to WriteInput only, and A2-2 gives WriteInput an InputResult outcome). The proof is provisional until the steward rules whether Cancelled is retained and which operation returns it.
- `Internal` (`core-testkit+edge`): OPEN STEWARD ITEM: A2-1 lists no sync Internal, and A2-2 gives WriteInput Internal as its only async error, but no clause names the edge that produces it (A5-3 item 2 allows an async code only through an edge). The proof is provisional until the steward names the edge or rules a unit proof.

## Points for the steward and the reviewer

- **Adoption.** Adoption ids are mapped to a new Core handle over the surviving in-process worker and the same storage edge (LC-12, AD-1). Only an adoption after a real host crash (`slow:real-host-crash`) is slow.
- **The C ABI** (Core section 13) has no ledger id, so it is not in this map.
- **Withdrawn.** `conf::a2_26_withdrawn` is a withdrawn clause. It has a proof of `hub-inproc` for completeness and proves no behavior.
- **Known FakeCore defect (steward ruling R-73, item 4).** FakeCore's session control `pty_input` gives the `op` of each segment as a JSON number (`botster-fake-core/src/control.rs`), where `Op` is a decimal string (Codec A.1). Since R-73 no driver reads `segments`, so the defect changes no result. FakeCore is frozen and keeps it.
